newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PICOP sees turnaround in election year.
newsitem.headline: PICOP sees turnaround in election year.

text.p: Paper manufacturer PICOP Resources Inc said on Tuesday it expected a financial turnaround next year because of the general elections slated in May.
"PICOP is eyeing a market rebound in 1998 with the onset of the national and local elections as it posted a 237 million peso loss in the last six months of 1996," it said in a statement.
PICOP posted a 718.6 million loss in the first semester of 1996.
The Philippines is scheduled to hold its presidential, national and congressional elections next year. Politicians use tonnes of posters and leaflets for their campaigning.
PICOP said the loss was due to declining paper prices in the international market which went to its all-time low last year.
A one-time expense was also incurred as 40 percent of its workforce availed of its voluntary retirement scheme.
PICOP is one of the largest fully integrated pulp and paper mills in the country.
